text:
Maya: Quick sync  did a 5-day hallway test on the pricing page calculator and tier names. Biggest surprise: people interpreted 'Dedicated' as hardware ownership, not just reserved throughput.

Carlos: Oof, makes sense. What naming options did you try?

Maya: We ran three labels in the test: 'Capacity Commit', 'Reserved Pro', and 'Commit+'. Sample n=60 across PMs/devs/infra folks. Key metrics: time-to-understand (self-reported), calculator use rate, and intent-to-contact-sales.

Eli: Any clear winner?

Maya: 'Capacity Commit' had the best clarity score (+22 vs baseline), and reduced "contact sales" by ~9%. But "Commit+" scored higher on perceived cost-savings (people thought + meant discounts).

June: Interesting. Does "Capacity Commit" feel too technical for non-technical buyers?

Maya: A few testers said it's slightly jargony. Proposed hybrid: use 'Reserved (Capacity Commit)' on the hero tier chip and 'Capacity Commit' in the calculator modal.

Carlos: I like hybrid. For the calc UX: tests show adding a simple scenario dropdown ("steady", "spiky") helped people pick config and see cost deltas. Can we add that?

Eli: Yes  and add a small variance band: "Estimate +/- 15% for short-term spikes". Also include a CTA: "Compare with Hosted rates" that toggles a side-by-side.

Maya: Draft FAQ lines below, keep it short so we don't overwhelm the page:

Q: What does "Capacity Commit" mean?
A: Its a monthly reserved capacity plan: you commit to a steady GPU capacity level for better unit pricing and predictable throughput. You can burst beyond your commit; burst usage follows published burst rates. See docs.redwood.ai/capacity-commit for billing details.

Q: Can I change my commitment mid-term?
A: Yes. Adjustments are supported via the Console or by contacting support; charges are prorated.

June: Add a one-liner about SLA differences vs Hosted. People need that up front.

Maya: Good call. I'll add "SLA-backed latency targets apply to Capacity Commit plans" next to the hero blurb.

ops-bot: experiment poll: 14 votes for 'Capacity Commit' (preferred clarity), 6 votes for 'Commit+', 4 for 'Reserved Pro'.

Carlos: OK. Next steps: Maya to push copy to /staging/pricing; I'll file eng ticket PRIC-482 for calc scenario toggle + side-by-side. Tagging @Eli for design QA.

Maya: Plan to ship FAQ update to staging tomorrow AM and run 1-week A/B split for calculator default label. If no objections by EOD Ill move forward. Thanks all :)
